items.title: Pulse wave velocity as a non-invasive discriminative marker of bone health in postmenopausal women.
items.abstract: Increased arterial stiffness has been linked to osteoporosis. This study evaluates Pulse Wave Velocity (PWV) as a discriminator of osteopenia and osteoporosis at the lumbar spine and femoral neck in postmenopausal women. In this cross-sectional study, arterial stiffness and bone mineral density (BMD) at the spine and femoral neck were assessed using carotid-to-femoral Pulse PWV and dual-energy x-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Eighteen premenopausal women (mean age 41.30±4.30 years) and forty-eight postmenopausal women (mean age 59.40±9.10 years) participated in the study. Osteoporosis (T-score ≤-2.5) and osteopenia (-2.5< T-score ≤-1) were defined by T-score criteria. Pearson's correlation results showed: PWV and femoral neck BMD (r = -0.439, P = 0.002), PWV and spine BMD (r =-0.358, P = 0.012), and PWV and menopausal duration (r = 0.381, P = 0.008). PWV demonstrated significant discriminative ability for femoral neck osteopenia [b = 0.6472, Wald = 5.717, Odds ratio (OR) = 1.910, P = 0.017, Area Under Curve (AUC) = 0.704], femoral neck osteoporosis (b = 0.7206, Wald = 5.838, OR = 2.056, P = 0.016, AUC = 0.758), spine osteopenia (b = 0.8489, Wald = 5.639, OR = 2.337, P = 0.018, AUC = 0.677), and spine osteoporosis (b = 1.0829, Wald = 8.269, OR = 2.953, P = 0.004, AUC = 0.804). PWV was inversely correlated with femoral neck and spine BMD, and positively correlated with menopausal duration. It serves as a significant discriminator of bone health, indicating increased odds of osteopenia and osteoporosis.

items.title: Support System as a Foundation for Self-Care Management Among Heart Failure Patients in Saudi Arabia.
items.abstract: Background and objective Various support system interventions have demonstrated efficacy in enhancing self-care management among patients with heart failure (HF) through a comprehensive understanding derived from diverse perspectives involving patients, caregivers, and healthcare providers (HCPs) in self-care practices. The objective of this study was to explore the self-care management needs of patients with HF and how caregivers and HCPs support these needs. Methods A qualitative approach was used to examine patients' experiences with HF. Purposive sampling was used to recruit 24 patients from a Saudi tertiary center between May 2024 and May 2025. Data collection involved semi-structured, face-to-face interviews about their understanding, practices, and challenges. The interviews were recorded, transcribed, and analyzed thematically. Results The findings highlight the importance of support systems as a foundation for self-care management among patients with HF. Participants with HF reported that their spouses were their primary caregivers. Most were satisfied with the care and communication provided by HCPs. Many did not exercise because of their condition. Most reported that HF-related costs were covered by the government, with some receiving financial aid. Others relied on family and relatives for support. Conclusions Support systems serve as a vital foundation for self-care management among patients with HF. Family caregivers, HCPs, and institutional resources all play crucial roles in ensuring comprehensive self-care management for patients with HF. Social media, newspapers, education initiatives, and free health screenings serve a significant role in raising public awareness and understanding of risk factors that predict HF.

items.title: Depressive symptoms and related factors in adults with heart failure: A multicenter cross-sectional study in northern Iran (2022-2023).
items.abstract: Depressive symptoms are frequent in patients with heart failure (HF), but estimates vary across settings. Clarifying their burden and related factors can inform integrated care. This study aimed to estimate the prevalence of depressive symptoms in adults with HF and identify associated factors. We conducted a multicenter cross-sectional study (June 2022-February 2023) in cardiology wards and outpatient clinics of three hospitals affiliated with Babol University of Medical Sciences, northern Iran. Consecutive adults (≥18 years) with cardiologist-confirmed HF completed the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D-17); a score >7 was considered indicative of clinically relevant depressive symptoms. Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics were recorded. Independent correlates of depressive symptoms were examined using multivariable logistic regression. Of 250 participants (mean age 60.3±15.1 years; 46.4% women), 51 (20.4%) had depressive symptoms (HAM-D-17 >7): mild 18.4%, moderate 1.6%, severe 0.4%. In unadjusted analyses, depressive symptoms were more common in women, in unemployed and unmarried participants, and in those with more advanced New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class. In multivariable models, female sex (OR 6.57, 95% CI 2.91-14.85) and higher NYHA class were associated with depressive symptoms (p<0.01), whereas left ventricular ejection fraction and HF etiology were not. Approximately one fifth of adults with HF had clinically relevant depressive symptoms, particularly women and patients with worse functional status. Routine screening and integrated psychosocial care should be incorporated into HF management, with special attention to patients in advanced NYHA classes.

items.title: Soluble E-selectin and QRISK3-based Cardiovascular Risk Assessment in Women with Polycystic Ovary Syndrome: A Prospective Case-control Study from India.
items.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is associated with metabolic abnormalities and increased long-term cardiovascular risk. Endothelial dysfunction is considered an early event in atherogenesis, and soluble E-selectin has been proposed as a marker of endothelial activation. However, its role in cardiovascular risk assessment in PCOS remains uncertain. The study aimed to compare circulating soluble E-selectin levels between women with PCOS and healthy controls and evaluate their association with metabolic parameters and QRISK3-based cardiovascular risk scores. Prospective hospital-based case-control study. Two hundred women with PCOS diagnosed according to the Rotterdam criteria and 50 age-matched healthy controls aged 18-40 years were enrolled. Clinical assessment, anthropometry, fasting blood glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, C-reactive protein and soluble E-selectin levels were evaluated. Estimated 10-year cardiovascular risk was calculated using the QRISK3 algorithm. Group comparisons, correlation analyses and multivariable linear regression were performed. Mean soluble E-selectin levels were comparable between women with PCOS and controls (0.61 ± 0.33 vs. 0.61 ± 0.29 ng/mL, P = 0.935). Within the PCOS group, soluble E-selectin correlated positively with HbA1c ( r = 0.326, P = 0.001) and fasting blood glucose ( r = 0.271, P = 0.001), while no significant associations were observed with anthropometric measures, lipid parameters, blood pressure or QRISK3 scores. In multivariable analysis, fasting blood glucose remained independently associated with soluble E-selectin. Soluble E-selectin levels did not differ between women with PCOS and controls and showed limited associations with cardiovascular risk factors. These findings do not support a major role for soluble E-selectin in cardiovascular risk assessment among young women with PCOS.

items.title: Kidney Outcomes in Structural Heart and Cardiac Surgical Trials: The Case for Longitudinal Endpoint Reporting.
items.abstract: The 2026 American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/American Diabetes Association/American Society of Nephrology guideline on cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome establishes kidney function as a determinant of cardiovascular risk rather than an adjacent comorbidity. Endpoint architecture in structural heart and cardiac surgical research has not been revised accordingly. Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 standardized acute kidney injury reporting with considerable rigor, staging injury on Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes serum creatinine criteria and requiring that new renal replacement therapy be reported discretely, but its scope is confined to the periprocedural window. No endpoint tracks filtration trajectory across follow-up, no threshold within the standard defines chronic kidney disease stage progression, and initiation of maintenance dialysis years after intervention has no reporting convention distinct from temporary replacement therapy in the immediate postoperative period. Pivotal trials consequently adjudicate cardiovascular outcomes for five years and kidney outcomes for 30 days. Registry evidence suggests the omission is consequential, with rapid filtration decline documented in more than a third of patients carrying preexisting kidney impairment within five years of cardiac surgery. This editorial argues for longitudinal reporting of estimated glomerular filtration rate, prespecification of stage progression and maintenance dialysis as adjudicated endpoints, and nephrology representation on trial steering committees with a defined role in kidney endpoint specification.

items.title: Universal CAR-T cell therapy: overcoming key hurdles on the path to off-the-shelf adoption.
items.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells have revolutionized oncology, delivering unprecedented clinical responses in patients with refractory B-cell malignancies. However, the traditional autologous paradigm - encompassing patient-specific leukapheresis, genetic modification, and extensive ex vivo expansion - imposes severe constraints on manufacturing timelines, costs, and global scalability. Allogeneic universal CAR-T (uCAR-T) reimagines this therapeutic unit as an "off-the-shelf" cellular medicine, utilizing healthy donor-derived cells produced in standardized batches to overcome the bottlenecks of individualized therapy. Over the past decade, the field has transitioned from foundational proof-of-concept studies in murine models to sophisticated early-phase human clinical trials. This review delineates the core biological and engineering principles of uCAR-T, specifically focusing on the genomic strategies employed to mitigate graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) and host-versus-graft disease (HvGD). We synthesize pivotal preclinical and clinical data alongside a comprehensive overview of the current clinical landscape. Furthermore, we highlight the primary translational hurdles remaining: ensuring durable CAR-T persistence and navigating the complexities of innate and adaptive immune rejection. We explore the potential for combination immunotherapies and specialized CAR architectures designed to penetrate solid tumors. Ultimately, uCAR-T is poised to democratize cellular immunotherapy, offering a scalable and transformative therapeutic perspective across diverse disease indications.

items.title: Intramedullary Spinal Cord Metastasis From Oligometastatic Melanoma of Unknown Primary Treated With Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy.
items.abstract: Intramedullary spinal cord metastasis (ISCM) is an uncommon and challenging clinical entity with no established consensus regarding its optimal management. A 37-year-old female presented with left-sided facial numbness, right leg paresthesia with decreased temperature sensation, and right lower extremity weakness. Investigations demonstrated two intracranial lesions and an ISCM at T10 to T11. Biopsy of the intracranial lesion confirmed melanoma. The patient was treated with stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to a dose of 30 Gy in 5 fractions to the ISCM and stereotactic radiosurgery to a dose of 20 Gy in a single fraction to the intracranial metastases. The spinal cord dose received by a 0.035 cc volume was limited to less than or equal to 30 Gy. No spinal cord planning organ-at-risk volume was used. SBRT was followed by combination ipilimumab and nivolumab for four cycles, then maintenance nivolumab thereafter. At 25 months post-SBRT, the treated lesions decreased in size. There were no severe acute or late radiation-related toxicities, and the patient remained fully ambulatory from presentation to last follow-up.

items.title: Late isolated renal fossa recurrence of clear cell renal cell carcinoma 15 Years post-nephrectomy: A case report and literature review.
items.abstract: Clear cell renal cell carcinoma is the most common type of renal carcinoma and among them ccRCC is most common. We report a case of a patient diagnosed with renal cell carcinoma (RCC), who exhibited no metastases at the time of nephrectomy but experienced recurrence in the renal fossa after 15 years. We report a late local recurrence of clear cell renal cell carcinoma after 15 year post radical nephrectomy. Lesion find in annual follow-up and initial biopsy show normal hepatic parenchyma we repeat biopsy and confirm local recurrence. The pathology after surgery confinm ccRCC and refer to oncologist for immunotherapy. In this case we emphasize for long term follow-up of RCC.

items.title: MRI-Based Radiomics Predicts FAP Expression and Immunosuppressive Tumor Microenvironment in Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: To develop a Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) -based radiomics-clinical model for noninvasive prediction of fibroblast activation protein (FAP) expression in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and to explore its association with tumor microenvironment (TME) characteristics and potential immunotherapy response. This retrospective study included 104 patients with HCC from the Fourth Hospital of Hebei Medical University, 31 external MRI cases from The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA), and 363 transcriptomic profiles from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Immunohistochemistry (IHC) assessed FAP expression. Tumor regions were manually segmented, and radiomics features were extracted using PyRadiomics. Multiple machine learning classifiers were used to construct and validate models for predicting FAP expression. Logistic regression was selected for its balanced performance between the training and validation cohorts, with the smallest area under the curve (AUC) difference among the five machine-learning algorithms. A radiomics-clinical combined model was further developed by integrating the radscore with clinical indicators. Radiogenomic analysis explored radscore-related transcriptomic features and immune infiltration characteristics. In the validation cohort, the AUC values of the intratumoral, peritumoral, and intratumoral + peritumoral radiomics models were 0.757, 0.502, and 0.784, respectively. The intratumoral + peritumoral model also achieved a sensitivity of 0.692 and a specificity of 0.788, indicating the best overall discriminatory performance among the three models. The radiomics-clinical combined model integrating the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), prognostic nutritional index (PNI), and radscore achieved an AUC of 0.816 in the validation cohort. Radscore-related transcriptomic modules identified 10 hub genes for risk stratification. Patients in the high-risk group exhibited a more pronounced immunosuppressive TME and poorer predicted benefit from immunotherapy. The MRI-based radiomics-clinical model effectively predicted FAP expression in HCC. Radscore reflected FAP-related immunosuppressive TME remodeling and may provide insights into potential immunotherapy response stratification, which requires further validation in independent immunotherapy-treated cohorts.

items.title: Bacterial Meningitis Following Robot-Assisted Radical Prostatectomy After Neoadjuvant Precision Oncology-Directed Therapy: A Case Report.
items.abstract: To our knowledge, bacterial meningitis following radical prostatectomy has not been previously reported. We present a 69-year-old male who had phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN)-deficient high-risk locoregional prostate cancer and received neoadjuvant leuprolide, abiraterone, prednisone, and capivasertib in the Single-Arm Phase II Study of Neoadjuvant Intensified Androgen Deprivation in Combination with protein kinase B (AKT) Inhibition (SNARE) trial and developed bacterial meningitis following robot-assisted radical prostatectomy. Diagnosis was established by cerebrospinal fluid analysis demonstrating leukocytosis and markedly elevated protein, although cultures were negative following prior antibiotic exposure. Though capivasertib is not considered overtly immunosuppressive, it is possible that a combination of androgen deprivation, low-dose steroids, alcohol use disorder, and surgical intervention resulted in a permissive immunologic environment for infection. This represents, to our knowledge, the first documented case of bacterial meningitis arising after radical prostatectomy. The relationship to his neoadjuvant therapy remains unclear.

items.title: Viral Hepatitis, Potential Aflatoxin B1 Exposure, and Projected Metabolic Risk Factors for Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Somalia: A Call for Integrated Prevention, Surveillance, and Research.
items.abstract: This commentary is a narrative synthesis of Somali, regional, and global evidence on hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) risk in Somalia; it does not report new epidemiological data, and claims are graded according to whether they are directly demonstrated in Somalia or inferred from broader African or global literature. Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a major cause of cancer mortality globally and presents a particularly difficult challenge in sub-Saharan Africa, where chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, hepatitis C virus (HCV), food-borne aflatoxin exposure, limited surveillance, and restricted access to curative treatment intersect. Somalia has no mature population-based cancer registry, yet available hospital-based evidence indicates that liver cancer is an important component of the national cancer burden. Directly documented Somali evidence is limited to hospital case series and to donor-, hospital-, and laboratory-based HBV studies: a Somali series of 268 patients with HCC documented a predominantly male population, a relatively young mean age, large tumors, and portal-vein thrombosis associated with poor prognostic features, and recent Mogadishu studies have shown continuing HBV transmission and important gaps in vaccination, testing, and linkage to care. By contrast, the contribution of aflatoxin B1 exposure and of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) to HCC in Somalia is not directly documented. No Somali biomonitoring, dietary-exposure, or MASLD-prevalence data exist; the discussion of these pathways in this commentary is therefore inferred from regional and global literature and should be read as a precautionary, hypothesis-generating projection of future risk rather than an established local driver of current disease. This commentary argues that Somalia should nonetheless not address viral, toxic, and metabolic exposures through isolated programs. An integrated, phased HCC prevention strategy should combine timely HBV birth-dose vaccination, maternal screening and antiviral prophylaxis, adult testing and treatment, HCV diagnosis and cure, precautionary food-safety surveillance for aflatoxins, metabolic-risk assessment embedded in liver care, risk-based liver ultrasound surveillance with alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) used only as an adjunct, strengthened diagnostic imaging and pathology, and a national liver-cancer registry. Locally led epidemiological and implementation research, including population-attributable-fraction scenario modelling and representativeness analyses of existing hospital series, is urgently needed to quantify the relative contribution of viral, toxic, and metabolic pathways and to identify feasible models for surveillance and referral in a resource-constrained setting.

items.title: Ademetionine 1,4-butanedisulfonate plus dexamethasone for cholestatic hepatitis: therapeutic efficacy and risk factors.
items.abstract: This retrospective study analyzes how patients with cholestatic hepatitis (CH) have responded to the dual-drug therapy consisting of Ademetionine 1,4-Butanedisulfonate (SAMe-BD) and Dexamethasone (DEX) and discusses the associated risk factors. First, we enrolled 128 CH patients admitted to our hospital (July 2022-July 2025), with 60 patients in the control group receiving SAMe-BD, and the remaining 68 cases in the research group receiving SAMe-BD+DEX. We then conducted comparative assessments of the following outcome measures: therapeutic efficacy, safety (nausea, diarrhea, insomnia, myalgia), symptom relief (fatigue, itching), liver function (total bilirubin [TBIL], alanine transaminase [ALT], alkaline phosphatase [ALP], γ-glutamyltransferase [GGT]), inflammation (interleukin [IL]-6, tumor necrosis factor [TNF-α]), fibrosis markers (type III procollagen peptide [PCIII], hyaluronic acid [HA], laminin [LN]), and serum lipid profiles (total cholesterol [TC], triglyceride [TG], low-density lipoprotein cholesterol [LDL-C]). Significant clinical correlates of therapeutic efficacy were analyzed using univariate and multivariate approaches. In the research group, markedly greater overall efficacy was observed compared to controls, alongside an equivalent incidence of total adverse reactions, significantly better symptom relief, and notably lower post-treatment levels of indices associated with liver function, inflammation, fibrosis, and blood lipids. Through further analysis, diabetes comorbidity, ALP, and therapeutic method were identified as independent determinants of therapeutic efficacy in CH patients. These findings support the role of SAMe-BD+DEX in significantly enhancing therapeutic effectiveness in CH patients. Also, the risk of treatment ineffectiveness is heightened in patients presenting with diabetes or high pre-treatment ALP, as well as in those using SAMe-BD alone.

items.title: Antidote activity of vitamin B 12 derivative compared with its original and aqua forms; in vitro and in vivo study.
items.abstract: Vitamin B 12 (VB12) - essential nutrient, required for detoxication of homocysteine, support of the myelinization in neural tissue and of the hematopoiesis. Certain drugs (such as antibiotics or antituberculosis drugs) result in deep deficiency of VB12. Using VB12 and its derivatives as antidotes is a promising direction in pharmacology, that allows compensation of the toxic effects of the drugs by nutraceuticals. In the present work, interactions of isoniazid (IZ) (a toxic drug, used in the pharmacotherapy of tuberculosis) with various VB12 derivatives were studied. An in vitro study in aqueous solutions with different pH values showed that the hydrophobic derivative of VB12-heptamethyl ester of aquacyanocobyric acid (ACm) promoted oxidation of IZ and contributed to reducing its hepatotoxicity. The effects of ACm were compared with VB12 and aquacobalamin in a rat model of acute IZ-induced hepatitis. IZ intoxication resulted in higher levels of aspartate aminotransferase (AST). Administration of VB12 and ACm normalized AST levels; treatment with aquacobalamin or ACm normalized total protein levels in blood serum. ACm malsoattenuated bilirubin levels in the blood. All VB12 derivatives significantly reduced lipid peroxidation, which was increased after IZ model was reproduced. Histological analysis confirmed the protective effects of these compounds on the rats' livers, kidneys, and brains: hepatocyte damage, inflammatory cell infiltration of liver tissues, acute ischemia of the renal cortex, and structural brain damage caused by IZ were all reduced. ACm had more positive effects on the liver than the other two compounds.
items.journal: Journal of food science and technology

items.title: Case Report: Henoch-Schönlein-like purpura as an unusual presentation of acute hepatitis E virus infection.
items.abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection is increasingly recognized as a cause of extrahepatic manifestations; however, cutaneous purpuric manifestations are exceptionally rare, with only one previous case of Henoch-Schönlein purpura (HSP) reported in association with acute HEV infection. This study describes the case of a 91-year-old man admitted with palpable purpura of the lower limbs, associated with jaundice, hypertransaminasemia, and cholestatic abnormalities. Molecular and serological assays were performed. Serological testing showed anti-HEV IgM and IgG positivity, and HEV RNA was detected in plasma at a viral load of 15,002 IU/mL. The patient reported consumption of wild-boar meat in the month preceding symptom onset. The purpura resolved spontaneously approximately 10 days after onset, and liver parameters progressively improved, with HEV RNA becoming undetectable at follow-up. Phylogenetic analysis of the patient-derived sequence identified the strain as HEV genotype 3f, belonging to the 3f2 subcluster. The patient-derived sequence showed similarity with European HEV-3f/3f2 human strains and with swine and wild boar strains, supporting a likely zoonotic food-borne origin. Plasma interleukin-6 (IL-6) was elevated at admission during the purpuric manifestation. To our knowledge, this is the first Italian report of an HSP-like purpura temporally associated with acute HEV genotype 3f infection. This case highlights that acute HEV infection may be considered in the differential diagnosis of patients presenting with palpable purpura, while emphasizing the exceptional rarity of this manifestation.

items.title: Profile of people treated for hepatitis C: a descriptive study, Pelotas, Brazil, 2023.
items.abstract: To describe the clinical-epidemiological profile of hepatitis C in individuals treated in Pelotas in 2023. This was a descriptive study, using data from medical records held at the Injectable Medication Administration and Follow-up Center. Characteristics of the individuals and the disease at the beginning of treatment were used, such as demographic variables, weight, origin of follow-up (public, private), viral load, genotyping, liver fibrosis staging, cirrhosis, human immunodeficiency virus coinfection, and treatment effectiveness. Analyses were stratified by sex, and differences were evaluated by Independent Samples t-test, Wilcoxon test or Fisher's exact test. 102 individuals were followed up, i.e. 59 males and 43 females, with mean ages of 52.4 and 57.1 years (p-value 0.037). Human immunodeficiency virus coinfection was 5.9%. 35% of patients assessed underwent genotyping, with type 1 being the most frequent in males and type 3 in females. Adherence among public sector health professionals to the Ministry of Health liver fibrosis staging protocol was higher than among those working in the private sector. One male and six females presented an advanced degree of liver fibrosis (Aspartate Aminotransferase-to-Platelet Ratio Index ≥2) (p-value 0.049) at the start of treatment. Most patients treated for hepatitis C were referred by the public system, with a low degree of fibrosis, although one-third presented some degree of cirrhosis. Disease staging was assessed primarily among public system users. Females were the majority regarding being at an advanced stage of the natural history of the disease. Sustained virological response occurred predominantly among males. Describir el perfil clínico-epidemiológico de la hepatitis C en personas tratadas en Pelotas en 2023. Estudio descriptivo, con datos de las historias clínicas del Centro de Aplicación y Monitoreo de Medicamentos Inyectables. Se analizaron las características de las personas y la enfermedad al inicio del tratamiento, como variables demográficas, peso, origen del seguimiento (público, privado), carga viral, genotipificación, estadificación de la fibrosis hepática, cirrosis, coinfección con el virus de la inmunodeficiencia humana y efectividad del tratamiento. Los análisis se estratificaron por sexo y las diferencias se evaluaron mediante la prueba t para muestras independientes, la prueba de Wilcoxon o la prueba exacta de Fisher. Se realizó un seguimiento de 102 personas, 59 hombres y 43 mujeres, con edades medias de 52,4 y 57,1 años (valor p 0,037). La coinfección con el virus de la inmunodeficiencia humana fue del 5,9%. Al 35% de los pacientes evaluados se les realizó genotipificación, siendo el tipo 1 el más frecuente en hombres y el tipo 3 en mujeres. La adherencia al protocolo de estadificación de la fibrosis hepática establecido por el Ministerio de Salud entre los profesionales del sector público fue mayor que entre los del sector privado. Un hombre y seis mujeres presentaron un grado avanzado de fibrosis hepática (cociente aspartato aminotransferasa/plaquetas ≥2) (valor p 0,049) al inicio del tratamiento. La mayoría de los pacientes tratados por hepatitis C provenían del sistema público, con un bajo grado de fibrosis, aunque un tercio presentó algún grado de cirrosis. La estadificación de la enfermedad se evaluó principalmente entre los usuarios de este sistema. La mayoría de las mujeres se encontraban en una etapa avanzada de la historia natural de la enfermedad. La respuesta virológica sostenida se observó predominantemente en los hombres.
items.journal: Epidemiologia e servicos de saude : revista do Sistema Unico de Saude do Brasil

items.title: Size-tuned gold nanoparticles for treating lethal bacterial pneumonia.
items.abstract: Targeted delivery and low toxicity are key considerations in the development of nanomaterials. Herein, we report a strategy to realize accumulation of antibacterial gold nanoparticles (GNPs) in the lungs via regulating particle size. We prepare two types of 3-amino-1,2,4-triazole-5-thiol-modified GNPs (A-GNPs) with distinct sizes: small A-GNPs (A-sGNPs) and large A-GNPs (A-lGNPs). The A-sGNPs preferentially accumulate in the lungs, instead of in the liver or kidneys. This targeting ability lowered their toxicity to the liver and kidneys. In contrast, the A-lGNPs exhibit the opposite distribution profile. The A-GNPs especially A-sGNPs show potent antibacterial effects against multidrug-resistant (MDR) Gram-negative bacteria. In a mouse model of pneumonia induced by MDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa , A-sGNPs achieve a 100% bacterial clearance rate in lung tissue and a 100% animal survival rate, demonstrating ideal therapeutic effects and low systemic toxicity in a size-dependent manner. Our work paves the way for developing nanomaterials with improved bioactivity and ameliorated side effects by tuning particle size, offering broad potential for biomedical applications.

items.title: Radiotherapy, inflammation, and the myeloid perspective.
items.abstract: Radiotherapy (RT) has long been regarded as a local treatment modality designed to eradicate tumor cells through targeted deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) damage and, more recently, as an in situ vaccine capable of triggering the abscopal effect. However, increasing evidence now defines RT as a systemic immune modulatory intervention that elicits both antitumor and tumor growth-promoting effects. The recently described "badscopal effect", the paradoxical progression or growth acceleration of non-irradiated disease associated with systemic immunosuppressive and growth-factor programs initiated by the irradiated lesion, highlights that RT may, under certain inflammatory and cellular contexts, foster immune tolerance or accelerate distant disease progression. Central to this duality is the host's capacity to integrate and balance antitumor and pro-tumor responses following RT. Unlike the relatively binary activation states often attributed to T cells, myeloid cells exhibit high plasticity, integrating signals of DNA damage, hypoxia, and tissue repair to direct the inflammatory responses that inhibit or promote tumor growth. In this review, we examine how RT induces dual inflammatory programs, as a partial explanation as to why classical abscopal models incompletely capture clinical practice and how myeloid plasticity emerges as a central determinant of systemic responses to RT, with important implications for the rational design of combination therapies.

items.title: Atezolizumab plus Bevacizumab with or without Transarterial Chemoembolization as First-Line Treatment for Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer Stage C Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Nationwide Multicenter Retrospective Study.
items.abstract: Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (Atezo/Bev) has been recommended globally for patients with Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer (BCLC) stage C hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC); however, this regimen has shown modest survival benefits. Therefore, this study aimed to assess the efficacy and safety of Atezo/Bev with or without transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) as first-line treatment for BCLC C HCC. This nationwide multicenter retrospective cohort study recruited patients with BCLC stage C HCC from 14 medical centres who received TACE combined with Atezo/Bev (TACE+Atezo/Bev) or Atezo/Bev alone as first-line treatment between October 2020 and January 2025. To mitigate potential confounding imbalances between groups, propensity score matching (PSM) and stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting (sIPTW) were applied. Overall survival (OS) was set as the primary endpoint, with progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), and safety assessed as the secondary endpoints. Of the 256 patients included in the analysis, 154 received TACE+Atezo/Bev and 102 received Atezo/Bev. After PSM, analysis of 96 patients per group showed that the TACE+Atezo/Bev group significantly extended the median OS (25.9 months vs. 15.2 months, p p p p p = 0.009; PSM cohort: 51.0% vs. 31.2%, p = 0.008; sIPTW cohort: 50.6% vs. 32.0%, p = 0.005). Moreover, Grade 3/4 adverse events (AEs) occurred in 60 patients (39.0%) in the TACE+Atezo/Bev group and 34 patients (33.3%) in the Atezo/Bev group. Compared with Atezo/Bev alone, TACE+Atezo/Bev may significantly improve ORR, PFS, and OS as first-line treatment for BCLC stage C HCC, while maintaining an acceptable safety profile.

items.title: Outcomes by Comorbidities with Tremelimumab and Durvalumab in the Randomized, Controlled Phase 3 HIMALAYA Study in Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
items.abstract: People with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) often have underlying comorbidities, which may impact prognosis and lead to safety challenges following treatment. This exploratory, post hoc analysis of the phase 3 HIMALAYA study (NCT03298451) assessed outcomes in participants with unresectable HCC and cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities at baseline. Participants with unresectable HCC were randomized to STRIDE (Single Tremelimumab Regular Interval Durvalumab), durvalumab monotherapy, or sorafenib. Comorbidities were based on medical history assessed at baseline and qualified using preferred terms from cardiovascular or metabolic Standardised Medical Dictionary for Regulatory Activities Queries. Overall survival (OS) rates were evaluated in participants with or without cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities within and by treatment group. The proportion of long-term survivors (alive ≥36 months post-randomization) and safety were assessed in participants with cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities. Data cutoffs: August 27, 2021 (primary analysis); January 23, 2023 (4-year updated analysis, OS, and serious treatment-related adverse events). Hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus were the most common cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidities, respectively. The 48-month OS rates with STRIDE were 28.0% and 21.7% in participants with and without cardiovascular comorbidities and 20.4% and 28.5% in those with and without metabolic comorbidities, respectively. In total, 28.2% of participants with cardiovascular comorbidities and 22.6% of participants with metabolic comorbidities experienced long-term survival with STRIDE. Safety in participants with cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities was generally consistent with all participants in the safety analysis set; no new safety signals were observed. OS benefits with STRIDE were similar in participants with vs. without cardiovascular or metabolic comorbidities, with manageable safety in participants with comorbidities. These results support the durable benefits of STRIDE in a broad population reflective of unresectable HCC globally.

items.title: Integrating Magnetic Resonance Imaging-Based Deep Learning and Radiomics to Predict Treatment Response in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Receiving Combined Systemic and Locoregional Therapies: A Multicenter Study.
items.abstract: Although combining systemic and locoregional therapies has improved outcomes for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), identifying appropriate candidates remains challenging because no reliable tool predicts response. This retrospective multicenter study enrolled 334 HCC patients who received first-line locoregional-systemic therapy from nine centers in China. Following automated tumor segmentation using nnU-Net on pretreatment contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging, predefined radiomics features were computationally extracted, and deep learning features were obtained via a ResNet convolutional neural network. Three types of predictive models for tumor response (radiomics, deep learning, and combined) were developed and validated on the training cohort ( n = 213), internal validation cohort (IVC, n = 53), and external validation cohort (EVC, n = 68). Performance was assessed using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) and net reclassification improvement (NRI). Associations of model with progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were evaluated. Among the three models (multi-sequence radiomics, multi-sequence deep learning, and combined), the combined model showed the best predictive performance in both the training (AUC: 0.997, 95% CI: 0.994-1.000) and validation cohorts (AUC of IVC 0.900, 95% CI: 0.806-0.994; AUC of EVC: 0.871, 95% CI: 0.790-0.951). The combined model demonstrated significantly improved predictive performance compared with the multi-sequence radiomic model (training NRI = 43.9%, p p = 0.038; EVC NRI = 3.2%, p = 0.806) and multi-sequence deep learning model (training NRI = 80.8%, IVC NRI = 72.7%, EVC NRI = 50.4%; all p < 0.05). Specifically, the combined model was significantly associated with both PFS and OS. The combined radiomics-deep learning model outperformed both single-modality models in predicting objective response and stratifying survival outcomes in unresectable HCC patients receiving combined systemic and locoregional therapy.
